data.body:
Epic AC verification, done before ticking.

AC1 — every child closed, each either deriving the mirrored value from its canonical source or adding a gate that fails on divergence. All 16 children are closed and each close passed the completion verifier, which is what AC1 names as the verification. Categorised: derivations are F1 (KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES), F2 (op-cert kinds), F3 (plan-review type partition), F4 (blocking relations), F6 (reducer statuses), F7 (composer types), F9 (source kinds), F11 (cross-session warn set) and florid-cookable-fly (bare-exempt set); divergence gates are F5 (MCP model drift), F8 (three-way relation parity), F10 (docs enumeration census), F12 (exit-codes conformance), F13 (gate step ids) and F14 (mutating-verb prose census).

ONE HONEST EXCEPTION, recorded rather than glossed: eagleeyed-commutable-mantisray (bc66) satisfies neither clause literally. It is the _cli/_registry.py validation split — a structural PREREQUISITE added mid-epic because _registry.py sat at exactly 800 lines and F11 could not add its Route flag without exceeding the cap. It remediates no mirror of its own. AC1 was written for the 14 inventory mirrors; bc66 and florid-cookable-fly were added during execution. florid-cookable-fly does derive, so it satisfies AC1 on its own terms; bc66 is an enabler and I am ticking AC1 with that exception stated rather than pretending it fits.

AC2 — no fix collapses a DISTINCT CONCEPT. Verified mechanically rather than by assertion: I took the union of files touched by all 14 merged epic commits (37 files) and intersected it with the files behind the inventory's nine rejected families. The intersection is EMPTY. In particular scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py was never touched, so F14 did not walk into the MUTATION_VERBS name-collision the inventory explicitly warns about — F14 touched only scripts/gen_cli_reference.py and the two prose copies.

Two places where the epic actively declined to collapse a distinct concept, which is AC2 working rather than merely not failing:
- F3: the gate found a seventh consumer at workflow_ops.py:108. I did NOT fold it in, because that set is the exempt set MINUS bug — a bug takes a light advisory review tier rather than a bare exempt PASS, so merging them would have silently deleted that tier. Split out as florid-cookable-fly and fixed separately with its own derivation.
- F11: WHICH verbs warn cross-session is a policy judgement; the ticket changed only that the spellings must BE route names, and pinned membership against the exact 14 to prove no policy moved.

Method note: my first attempt at the AC2 census returned zero files, which I nearly reported as 'no intersection'. It was an empty result from a broken git invocation, not evidence. Re-ran it correctly, and then found my SHA list covered only 11 of the 14 commits and completed it — the missing three included F11, whose _execute.py edit had been absent from the census.
